"""Sparse refill-failure cost pressure.

Mechanism: an elevated effective-versus-quoted execution cost becomes a
continuation signal when directional flow is accompanied by a failure of the
visible book to replenish.  This identifies sparse-liquidity price formation:
a latent execution schedule consumes a temporarily thin side of the book, and
prices adjust gradually while dealers rebuild displayed depth.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cost_wedge_surprise(
    effective_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    quoted_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    active: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Robust, causal positive surprise in realized execution cost."""
    ratio = effective_spread / quoted_spread.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    raw = np.log(ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(active)
    center = raw.rolling(150, min_periods=45).median()
    mad = (raw - center).abs().rolling(150, min_periods=45).median()
    z = (raw - center) / (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return z.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0).fillna(0.0).where(active, 0.0)


def _signed_persistent_pressure(
    trade: pd.DataFrame,
    order_flow: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slow marked-flow kernel, scaled robustly within each ticker."""
    trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    flow_scale = order_flow.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normalized_trade = np.tanh(trade / trade_scale).fillna(0.0)
    normalized_flow = np.tanh(order_flow / flow_scale).fillna(0.0)
    impulse = 0.60 * normalized_trade + 0.40 * normalized_flow
    signed = impulse.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    absolute = impulse.abs().ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    coherence = (signed.abs() / absolute.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    return (signed * coherence).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class SparseRefillFailureCostPressure(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "sparse_refill_failure_cost_pressure"
    name = "Sparse Refill Failure Cost Pressure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of persistent signed execution-cost pressure, "
        "gated by aligned effective-book imbalance and a displayed-depth "
        "shortfall relative to its slow replenishment baseline."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = [
        "close", "volume", "trade", "orderFlow", "spread", "effSpread",
        "depth", "effLobImb",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        order_flow = data["orderFlow"].fillna(0.0)
        quoted = data["spread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective = data["effSpread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        depth = data["depth"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective_imbalance = data["effLobImb"].fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        active = (volume > 0.0) & (quoted > 0.0) & (effective > 0.0) & (depth > 0.0)
        wedge = _cost_wedge_surprise(effective, quoted, active)
        pressure = _signed_persistent_pressure(trade, order_flow)

        short_depth = depth.ewm(halflife=12, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
        slow_depth = depth.ewm(halflife=90, adjust=False, min_periods=35).mean()
        refill_deficit = (1.0 - short_depth / slow_depth.replace(0.0, np.nan))
        refill_deficit = refill_deficit.clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.90).fillna(0.0)

        book_state = effective_imbalance.ewm(halflife=8, adjust=False, min_periods=6).mean()
        alignment = (np.sign(pressure) * book_state).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
        persistent_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean().fillna(0.0)

        raw = pressure * persistent_cost * refill_deficit * alignment
        eligible = active & (refill_deficit > 0.02) & (alignment > 0.05)
        signal = rank(raw.where(eligible)).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Sparse Refill Failure Cost Pressure
programs.trading_idea: Persistent effective-cost wedges are informative only when the visible book is failing to replenish after directional trading pressure, making price formation locally sparse rather than merely expensive. A buy (sell) program should continue to move prices when its signed trade/order-flow kernel agrees with effective-book imbalance and total displayed depth remains below its slower baseline. This is falsified if, conditional on the parent-style persistent cost state, depth-deficit and aligned-book episodes do not have stronger 60-bar continuation than adequately replenished episodes; the edge persists because the remaining parent order and replenishment capacity are only partially visible to arbitrageurs.
programs.description: Ranks directionally persistent marked execution-cost pressure only when effective LOB imbalance agrees with the pressure and displayed depth is materially below its slow replenishment baseline.

programs.code:
"""The ordering of a price impulse and a liquidity withdrawal contains information that terminal returns and contemporaneous spreads discard. When one-sided order-book pressure develops while spreads progressively widen before the price has fully adjusted, liquidity suppliers appear to be anticipating adverse selection rather than merely reacting to a completed move, favoring continuation. The signal should fail when the signed spread-return loop has no incremental directional power after controlling for current imbalance and realized range, indicating that it is just a volatility proxy."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _closed_path_area(
    x: pd.DataFrame, y: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal oriented area of the trailing closed x/y path.

    The path is closed by a straight line from its current endpoint to its
    trailing-window start.  This makes the shoelace area translation invariant
    and captures whether spread movement led or lagged the return trajectory.
    """
    edge_cross = x.shift(1) * y - y.shift(1) * x
    path_integral = edge_cross.rolling(window - 1, min_periods=window - 1).sum()
    start_x = x.shift(window - 1)
    start_y = y.shift(window - 1)
    closing_edge = x * start_y - y * start_x
    return 0.5 * (path_integral + closing_edge)


def _rolling_residual_two_controls(
    y: pd.DataFrame,
    x1: pd.DataFrame,
    x2: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Current residual from a causal rolling OLS with intercept and two controls."""
    y_bar = y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    x1_bar = x1.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    x2_bar = x2.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()

    yd = y - y_bar
    x1d = x1 - x1_bar
    x2d = x2 - x2_bar

    s11 = (x1d * x1d).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    s22 = (x2d * x2d).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    s12 = (x1d * x2d).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    s1y = (x1d * yd).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    s2y = (x2d * yd).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()

    determinant = s11 * s22 - s12 * s12
    safe_det = determinant.where(determinant.abs() > 1.0e-12)
    beta1 = (s1y * s22 - s2y * s12) / safe_det
    beta2 = (s2y * s11 - s1y * s12) / safe_det
    return yd - beta1 * x1d - beta2 * x2d


@register_factor
class SpreadReturnHysteresisPressureSignal(BaseFactor):
    """Continuation signal from pressure-aligned spread-return hysteresis loops."""

    factor_id = "spread_return_hysteresis_pressure_signal"
    name = "Spread-Return Hysteresis Pressure Signal"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of a causal spread-return loop whose orientation "
        "predicts the direction implied by both signed trade and effective-book "
        "imbalance, after removing rolling imbalance and realized-range effects."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "high",
        "low",
        "volume",
        "trade",
        "spread",
        "effLobImb",
        "depth",
        "nbEvents",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        high = data["high"].astype(float)
        low = data["low"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        trade = data["trade"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        spread = data["spread"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        eff_imb = data["effLobImb"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        depth = data["depth"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        events = data["nbEvents"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        standard_window = 30
        path_window = 18
        control_window = 60

        safe_close = close.where(close > 0.0)
        log_return = np.log(safe_close).diff()
        return_scale = log_return.rolling(
            standard_window, min_periods=standard_window
        ).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized_return = (log_return / return_scale).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

        safe_spread = spread.where(spread > 0.0)
        log_spread_change = np.log(safe_spread).diff()
        spread_scale = log_spread_change.rolling(
            standard_window, min_periods=standard_window
        ).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        standardized_spread_change = (log_spread_change / spread_scale).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

        cumulative_return = standardized_return.cumsum()
        cumulative_spread = standardized_spread_change.cumsum()
        raw_area = _closed_path_area(cumulative_return, cumulative_spread, path_window)

        path_energy = (
            standardized_return.pow(2) + standardized_spread_change.pow(2)
        ).rolling(path_window, min_periods=path_window).sum()
        loop_score = raw_area / path_energy.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        safe_volume = volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        trade_imb = (trade / safe_volume).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        trade_imb = trade_imb.fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        safe_range_close = safe_close.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        realized_range = ((high - low).abs() / safe_range_close).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)
        range_mean = realized_range.rolling(
            standard_window, min_periods=standard_window
        ).mean()
        range_std = realized_range.rolling(
            standard_window, min_periods=standard_window
        ).std().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        range_z = ((realized_range - range_mean) / range_std).replace(
            [np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan
        ).fillna(0.0)

        incremental_loop = _rolling_residual_two_controls(
            loop_score, eff_imb, range_z, control_window
        )

        predicted_direction = -incremental_loop
        aligned = (predicted_direction * trade_imb > 0.0) & (
            predicted_direction * eff_imb > 0.0
        )
        pressure_strength = np.sqrt(trade_imb.abs() * eff_imb.abs())

        depth_baseline = depth.rolling(standard_window, min_periods=1).mean()
        event_baseline = events.rolling(standard_window, min_periods=1).mean()
        depth_reliability = depth / (depth + depth_baseline).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        event_reliability = events / (events + event_baseline).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        reliability = np.sqrt(
            depth_reliability.fillna(0.0) * event_reliability.fillna(0.0)
        )

        directional_signal = (
            predicted_direction
            * pressure_strength
            * reliability
        ).where(aligned, 0.0)

        return rank(directional_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Spread-Return Hysteresis Pressure Signal
programs.trading_idea: The ordering of a price impulse and a liquidity withdrawal contains information that terminal returns and contemporaneous spreads discard. When one-sided order-book pressure develops while spreads progressively widen before the price has fully adjusted, liquidity suppliers appear to be anticipating adverse selection rather than merely reacting to a completed move, favoring continuation. The signal should fail when the signed spread-return loop has no incremental directional power after controlling for current imbalance and realized range, indicating that it is just a volatility proxy.
programs.description: Over a causal short rolling path, compute the oriented area of the standardized cumulative signed return and standardized spread trajectory, a discrete hysteresis/lead-lag measure. Retain only loops whose orientation agrees with signed trade and effective-book imbalance, and normalize by depth and event intensity so that mechanical quote noise receives little weight.

programs.code:
"""Event-clock clustered flow completion.

Mechanism: a directional sequence of trades occurring in an over-dispersed burst
of LOB events is more likely to be an unfinished, self-exciting execution
program than an isolated liquidity-taking trade.  Same-side effective-book
imbalance confirms that the burst is consuming available liquidity rather than
being passively absorbed; subsequent returns should continue in the flow
direction while the execution episode completes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _event_fano(events: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing event-count Fano factor; values above one indicate clustering.

    This is causal because both moments use only the trailing window ending at
'the current bar.'
    """
    mean_events = events.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    var_events = events.rolling(window, min_periods=window).var()
    return var_events / mean_events.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class EventClockClusteredFlowCompletion(BaseFactor):
    """Directional pressure from self-exciting event-clock activity bursts."""

    factor_id = "event_clock_clustered_flow_completion"
    name = "Event-Clock Clustered Flow Completion"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks signed trade pressure confirmed by effective LOB imbalance, "
        "with weight only in regimes of accelerating and over-dispersed "
        "LOB-event activity."
    )
    window_length = 90
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "trade", "effLobImb", "nbEvents"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        trade = data["trade"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        imb = data["effLobImb"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        events = data["nbEvents"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        short_window = 6
        persistence_window = 30
        activity_window = 60

        short_volume = volume.rolling(short_window, min_periods=short_window).sum()
        short_flow = trade.rolling(short_window, min_periods=short_window).sum()
        flow_impulse = short_flow / short_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        long_volume = volume.rolling(persistence_window, min_periods=persistence_window).sum()
        long_flow = trade.rolling(persistence_window, min_periods=persistence_window).sum()
        persistent_flow = long_flow / long_volume.replace(0.0, np.nan)

        mean_imb = imb.rolling(short_window, min_periods=short_window).mean()
        directional_agreement = (
            (flow_impulse * persistent_flow > 0.0)
            & (flow_impulse * mean_imb > 0.0)
        )

        short_activity = events.rolling(short_window, min_periods=short_window).mean()
        activity_mean = events.rolling(activity_window, min_periods=activity_window).mean()
        activity_std = events.rolling(activity_window, min_periods=activity_window).std()
        activity_acceleration = (
            (short_activity - activity_mean) / activity_std.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        )
        acceleration_gate = activity_acceleration.clip(lower=0.0)

        fano = _event_fano(events, persistence_window)
        clustering_gate = (fano - 1.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        persistence_strength = persistent_flow.abs().clip(upper=1.0)
        book_strength = mean_imb.abs().clip(upper=1.0)
        raw_signal = (
            flow_impulse
            * persistence_strength
            * np.sqrt(book_strength)
            * acceleration_gate
            * clustering_gate
        ).where(directional_agreement, 0.0)

        raw_signal = raw_signal.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return rank(raw_signal).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.0)
programs.name: Event-Clock Clustered Flow Completion
programs.trading_idea: Directional trading pressure should be more informative when it arrives in an over-dispersed burst of book events rather than at a smooth clock-time rate: clustered event arrivals are consistent with self-exciting execution and an unfinished parent-order sequence. The child goes long clustered buy pressure and short clustered sell pressure only when the effective book imbalance confirms the same direction, so it distinguishes persistent execution from isolated aggressive trades. This is falsifiable: conditional on equal short-horizon trade imbalance and current book imbalance, the signal should predict 60-bar returns only when event-count dispersion and recent event-clock acceleration are elevated. The edge can persist because identifying an incomplete execution episode does not eliminate the inventory and adverse-selection cost borne by liquidity providers who must absorb it immediately.
programs.description: Computes a signed short-horizon trade-flow impulse, confirmed by effective book imbalance, and scales it by event-clock acceleration and over-dispersion of LOB-event counts. The factor favors directional flow occurring in unusually clustered, self-exciting activity regimes.

programs.code:
"""Common-shock transmission deficit across order flow and returns.

Mechanism: synchronized trading shocks first create commonality in signed order
flow and event activity.  Names whose flow is already coupled to the peer shock
but whose returns have not yet acquired the corresponding peer correlation are
interpreted as delayed recipients of the common repricing pressure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _leave_one_out_mean(panel: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cross-sectional mean excluding the focal name at each timestamp."""
    count = panel.notna().sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    total = panel.sum(axis=1, skipna=True)
    denominator = count - 1.0
    peer = panel.rsub(total, axis=0).div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan), axis=0)
    return peer.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


def _rolling_corr_to_peer(
    values: pd.DataFrame, peer: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal rolling per-name correlation with a corresponding peer series."""
    x_mean = values.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    y_mean = peer.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    xy_mean = (values * peer).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean()
    covariance = xy_mean - x_mean * y_mean
    x_var = (values * values).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean() - x_mean * x_mean
    y_var = (peer * peer).rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean() - y_mean * y_mean
    denominator = np.sqrt(x_var.clip(lower=0.0) * y_var.clip(lower=0.0))
    return (covariance / denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class CommonModeCorrelationLeadDeficit(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "common_mode_correlation_lead_deficit"
    name = "Common-Mode Correlation Lead Deficit"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks stocks whose signed trade flow is more correlated with the "
        "leave-one-out peer flow shock than their returns are with peer returns, "
        "signed by a confirmed common-flow impulse and gated by broad activity."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = ["close", "trade", "nbEvents"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        events = data["nbEvents"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        trade_scale = trade.abs().ewm(halflife=30.0, adjust=False).mean()
        flow = (trade / trade_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-5.0, 5.0).fillna(0.0)
        own_flow = flow.ewm(halflife=5.0, adjust=False).mean()
        peer_flow = _leave_one_out_mean(flow)

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        peer_ret = _leave_one_out_mean(ret)

        flow_corr = _rolling_corr_to_peer(flow, peer_flow, 48)
        return_corr = _rolling_corr_to_peer(ret, peer_ret, 48)
        transmission_deficit = (flow_corr - return_corr).clip(lower=0.0, upper=2.0)

        common_impulse = peer_flow.ewm(halflife=5.0, adjust=False).mean().clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        directional_participation = (
            np.sign(common_impulse) * own_flow
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)

        event_baseline = events.ewm(halflife=60.0, adjust=False).mean()
        event_ratio = events / event_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        broad_activity = _leave_one_out_mean(event_ratio.fillna(0.0)).ewm(
            halflife=5.0, adjust=False
        ).mean().clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        activity_gate = (broad_activity / (1.0 + broad_activity)).fillna(0.0)

        score = (
            common_impulse
            * transmission_deficit
            * directional_participation
            * activity_gate
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        return rank(score).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Common-Mode Correlation Lead Deficit
programs.trading_idea: Broad, synchronized order-flow shocks propagate through trading activity before they fully propagate through return correlations: a name can be strongly coupled to the peer flow shock while its price remains weakly coupled to peer returns. The signal buys (sells) confirmed participants in a positive (negative) common flow episode whose flow-correlation exceeds their return-correlation, interpreting this gap as incomplete common-shock transmission rather than terminal imbalance. This is falsified if the flow-minus-return correlation deficit does not predict directionally aligned 60-bar returns after conditioning on common flow direction and event intensity. The edge can persist because liquidity suppliers and execution algorithms respond locally to a system-wide shock, while cross-name price synchronization requires slower inventory rebalancing, hedging, and cross-venue arbitrage.
programs.description: Computes each stock's trailing correlation with leave-one-out peer flow and subtracts its correlation with leave-one-out peer returns. It multiplies this transmission deficit by the signed common flow impulse, confirmed own participation, and elevated market-wide event activity.

programs.code:
"""Causal-arrow flow temperature drift.

Mechanism: order flow is informative when the local time direction runs from
trades to prices, rather than from prior price changes to reactive trading.
A large directed response combined with a low residual return temperature
indicates that a latent execution program is transmitting information through
the book; persistent signed flow then predicts gradual price adjustment.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _causal_transmission_state(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    imbalance: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Trailing flow-to-price asymmetry and explained-variance weight.

    All correlations use only observations at or before the current bar.  The
    first correlation measures response to a positive-lag flow impulse, while
    the second is the reverse price-to-flow feedback channel.
    """
    lag_flow = imbalance.shift(1)
    lag_ret = ret.shift(1)

    response = ret.rolling(150, min_periods=55).corr(lag_flow)
    feedback = imbalance.rolling(150, min_periods=55).corr(lag_ret)
    arrow = (response - feedback).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

    flow_var = lag_flow.rolling(150, min_periods=55).var()
    covar = ret.rolling(150, min_periods=55).cov(lag_flow)
    beta = covar / flow_var.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    residual = ret - beta * lag_flow
    total_var = ret.rolling(150, min_periods=55).var()
    residual_var = residual.rolling(150, min_periods=55).var()
    explained_share = (1.0 - residual_var / total_var.replace(0.0, np.nan))
    explained_share = explained_share.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)

    state = arrow.clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0) * np.sqrt(explained_share)
    return state.ewm(halflife=15, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean().fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class CausalArrowFlowTemperatureDrift(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "causal_arrow_flow_temperature_drift"
    name = "Causal Arrow Flow Temperature Drift"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks persistent signed trade pressure only when trailing lagged-flow "
        "response exceeds reverse price-feedback and lagged flow explains a "
        "substantial share of local return variation."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "trade", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)

        valid_price = close.where(close > 0.0)
        ret = np.log(valid_price).diff().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        scale = trade.abs().rolling(90, min_periods=25).median()
        imbalance = np.tanh(trade / scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).fillna(0.0)
        persistent_flow = imbalance.ewm(
            halflife=12, adjust=False, min_periods=8
        ).mean().fillna(0.0)

        transmission = _causal_transmission_state(ret, imbalance)
        active = (volume > 0.0) & scale.notna()
        raw = (persistent_flow * transmission).where(active)
        signal = rank(raw).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Causal Arrow Flow Temperature Drift
programs.trading_idea: The signal identifies episodes in which lagged signed trading statistically drives subsequent price changes more strongly than past price changes drive subsequent trading, a measurable time-arrow asymmetry in the local order-flow/price system. It is strongest when this causal transmission explains a large share of return variance, indicating low residual microstructure temperature rather than noisy two-way feedback; persistent flow in that state should continue to move prices over the fixed 60-bar horizon. This is falsified if flow-directed response asymmetry does not separate future continuation from equally active price-reactive episodes; the edge persists because the directed-response state requires a trailing sample to estimate and reflects temporarily latent institutional demand that cannot be costlessly front-run at scale.
programs.description: Computes a trailing directed-response asymmetry: correlation of current returns with lagged normalized trade imbalance minus correlation of current imbalance with lagged returns. It multiplies persistent signed trade pressure by this positive causal asymmetry and by the trailing variance share explained by lagged flow.

programs.code:
"""Marked excitation conditioned on sparse refill failure.

Mechanism: persistent directionally marked execution costs reveal an unfinished
metaorder, while a depth deficit and aligned effective-book imbalance reveal
that the visible book is not replenishing enough to absorb it.  The joint
state identifies sparse-liquidity price formation and continuation rather than
an isolated expensive execution event.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _cost_surprise(
    effective_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    quoted_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    active: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust positive surprise in realized execution cost."""
    ratio = effective_spread / quoted_spread.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    raw = np.log(ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(active)
    center = raw.rolling(150, min_periods=45).median()
    mad = (raw - center).abs().rolling(150, min_periods=45).median()
    zscore = (raw - center) / (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return zscore.clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0).fillna(0.0).where(active, 0.0)


def _marked_excitation(
    wedge: pd.DataFrame,
    trade: pd.DataFrame,
    order_flow: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slow signed marked-flow intensity with persistence and coherence."""
    trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    flow_scale = order_flow.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    normalized_trade = np.tanh(trade / trade_scale).fillna(0.0)
    normalized_flow = np.tanh(order_flow / flow_scale).fillna(0.0)
    signed_flow = (0.60 * normalized_trade + 0.40 * normalized_flow).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

    marked = wedge * signed_flow
    slow_signed = marked.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    slow_absolute = marked.abs().ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    coherence = (slow_signed.abs() / slow_absolute.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    short_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    long_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=90, adjust=False, min_periods=30).mean()
    elevation = (short_cost / long_cost.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
    elevation = elevation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

    return (slow_signed * coherence * elevation).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


@register_factor
class MarkedExcitationSparseRefillState(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "marked_excitation_sparse_refill_state"
    name = "Marked Excitation Sparse Refill State"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks persistent signed cost excitation only when displayed depth is "
        "below its slow refill baseline and effective-book imbalance agrees "
        "with the marked-flow direction."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = [
        "close", "volume", "trade", "orderFlow", "spread", "effSpread",
        "depth", "effLobImb",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        order_flow = data["orderFlow"].fillna(0.0)
        quoted = data["spread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective = data["effSpread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        depth = data["depth"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective_imbalance = data["effLobImb"].fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        active = (volume > 0.0) & (quoted > 0.0) & (effective > 0.0) & (depth > 0.0)
        wedge = _cost_surprise(effective, quoted, active)
        excitation = _marked_excitation(wedge, trade, order_flow)

        short_depth = depth.ewm(halflife=12, adjust=False, min_periods=10).mean()
        slow_depth = depth.ewm(halflife=90, adjust=False, min_periods=35).mean()
        refill_deficit = 1.0 - short_depth / slow_depth.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        refill_deficit = refill_deficit.clip(lower=0.0, upper=0.90).fillna(0.0)

        book_state = effective_imbalance.ewm(halflife=8, adjust=False, min_periods=6).mean()
        alignment = (np.sign(excitation) * book_state).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        excitation_floor = excitation.abs().rolling(120, min_periods=45).quantile(0.60)
        persistent_state = excitation.abs() >= excitation_floor.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        eligible = active & persistent_state & (refill_deficit > 0.02) & (alignment > 0.05)

        raw = excitation * refill_deficit * alignment
        signal = rank(raw.where(eligible)).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Marked Excitation Sparse Refill State
programs.trading_idea: Persistent marked execution-cost excitation identifies an unfinished, directionally coherent metaorder, but Parent B alone also admits costly episodes that can be absorbed by a healthy book. This child activates that excitation only when displayed depth remains below its replenishment baseline and effective-book imbalance agrees with the metaorder direction. The interaction isolates the state in which latent demand is still consuming scarce liquidity while dealers have not restored queue capacity, creating continuation over the 60-bar horizon that neither elevated cost persistence nor sparse depth alone can identify.
programs.description: Computes a robust effective-versus-quoted cost surprise, marks it by persistent normalized signed trade and order flow, and retains it only during sustained excitation. The signed signal is then gated by a short-versus-slow depth refill deficit and aligned effective LOB imbalance before cross-sectional ranking.

programs.code:
"""Persistent cost fragility confirmation: unfinished flow under worsening absorption.

Mechanism: a slowly persistent, directionally marked effective-cost state is
interpreted as latent split-order pressure only when a fresh cost wedge and the
visible book still confirm that direction under deteriorating liquidity.  The
state-dependent interaction distinguishes continuing adverse selection from a
completed sweep that has already been replenished.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

def _cost_wedge(effective_spread: pd.DataFrame, quoted_spread: pd.DataFrame, active: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust positive surprise in effective relative to quoted cost."""
    ratio = effective_spread / quoted_spread.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    raw = np.log(ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(active)
    center = raw.rolling(window, min_periods=30).median()
    mad = (raw - center).abs().rolling(window, min_periods=30).median()
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return ((raw - center) / scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0).fillna(0.0).where(active, 0.0)

def _persistent_marked_state(wedge: pd.DataFrame, trade: pd.DataFrame, order_flow: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slow signed cost kernel, attenuated when historical marks alternate."""
    trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(62, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    flow_scale = order_flow.abs().rolling(62, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    direction = (0.6 * np.tanh(trade / trade_scale).fillna(0.0) + 0.4 * np.tanh(order_flow / flow_scale).fillna(0.0)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
    marked = wedge * direction
    signed_kernel = marked.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    absolute_kernel = marked.abs().ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    coherence = (signed_kernel.abs() / absolute_kernel.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)
    short_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    long_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=90, adjust=False, min_periods=30).mean()
    elevation = (short_cost / long_cost.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0).clip(0.0, 3.0).fillna(0.0)
    return (signed_kernel * coherence * elevation).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

def _fresh_fragile_confirmation(wedge: pd.DataFrame, trade: pd.DataFrame, order_flow: pd.DataFrame, lob_imbalance: pd.DataFrame, effective_lob_imbalance: pd.DataFrame, depth: pd.DataFrame, trade_liquidity: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Current directional pressure magnified only by impaired absorption."""
    trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(62, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    flow_scale = order_flow.abs().rolling(59, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    consensus = 0.35 * np.tanh(trade / trade_scale).fillna(0.0) + 0.3 * np.tanh(order_flow / flow_scale).fillna(0.0) + 0.15 * lob_imbalance.clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0) + 0.2 * effective_lob_imbalance.clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
    directional_pressure = consensus * consensus.abs()
    prior_depth = depth.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    depth_stress = (1.0 - depth / prior_depth).clip(0.0, 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
    liquid_base = trade_liquidity.rolling(56, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    liquidity_deficit = ((liquid_base - trade_liquidity) / liquid_base).clip(0.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)
    fragility = 1.0 + 0.5 * depth_stress + 0.5 * liquidity_deficit
    return (wedge * directional_pressure * fragility).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

@register_factor
class PersistentCostFragilityConfirmation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = 'persistent_cost_fragility_confirmation_j'
    name = 'Persistent Cost Fragility Confirmation'
    category = 'microstructure'
    description = 'Ranks persistent signed execution-cost excitation only when a fresh fragile-liquidity cost-pressure event confirms its direction through trades, order flow, and visible book imbalance.'
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ['close', 'volume', 'trade', 'orderFlow', 'spread', 'effSpread', 'lobImb', 'effLobImb', 'depth', 'trdLiq']
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data['close']
        volume = data['volume'].fillna(0.0)
        trade = data['trade'].fillna(0.0)
        order_flow = data['orderFlow'].fillna(0.0)
        quoted_spread = data['spread'].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective_spread = data['effSpread'].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        lob_imbalance = data['lobImb'].fillna(0.0)
        effective_lob_imbalance = data['effLobImb'].fillna(0.0)
        depth = data['depth'].fillna(0.0)
        trade_liquidity = data['trdLiq'].fillna(0.0)
        active = (volume > 0.0) & (quoted_spread > 0.0) & (effective_spread > 0.0)
        wedge = _cost_wedge(effective_spread, quoted_spread, active, 120)
        persistent = _persistent_marked_state(wedge, trade, order_flow)
        confirmation = _fresh_fragile_confirmation(wedge, trade, order_flow, lob_imbalance, effective_lob_imbalance, depth, trade_liquidity)
        same_direction = (np.sign(persistent) * np.sign(confirmation) + 1.0) / 2.0
        same_direction = same_direction.where(confirmation != 0.0, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        signal = persistent * confirmation.abs() * same_direction
        return rank(signal.where(active)).fillna(0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: Persistent directionally marked execution-cost excitation identifies a latent metaorder state, but by itself it can include flow that dealers have already absorbed. The child conditions that slow state on a fresh effective-versus-quoted cost wedge whose trade, order-flow, and displayed-book pressure still agree with the historical direction while depth and trade liquidity deteriorate. This interaction isolates the subset of persistent flow for which liquidity supply is actively becoming less able to absorb the remaining schedule, creating a continuation hazard that neither an isolated fragile-cost event nor persistent flow without current confirmation identifies alone.

The output is the cross-sectional rank of this state-dependent continuation pressure.

"""Delayed transmission of common order-flow shocks through sparse active queues.

Mechanism: a market-wide signed-flow impulse reaches stocks with positive flow
exposure unevenly.  When an actively updating queue is thin, the stock's
short-run return can lag its causally estimated response to the common shock;
the response debt should be paid as liquidity is replenished over the next
several minutes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _broadcast_series(series: pd.Series, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Broadcast a time series across the ticker panel without changing time order."""
    values = np.tile(series.to_numpy(dtype=float)[:, None], (1, len(columns)))
    return pd.DataFrame(values, index=series.index, columns=columns)


def _rolling_beta(
    y: pd.DataFrame, x: pd.DataFrame, window: int
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal trailing beta of y on x, with a zero-variance guard."""
    covariance = y.rolling(window, min_periods=window).cov(x)
    variance = x.rolling(window, min_periods=window).var()
    return covariance / variance.replace(0.0, np.nan)


@register_factor
class CommonShockSparseQueueDeferredTransmission(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "common_shock_sparse_queue_deferred_transmission"
    name = "Common-Shock Sparse Queue Transmission"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks the unpriced return response to a robust common signed-trade "
        "shock, conditional on positive historical flow exposure and an "
        "actively updating but sparse displayed queue."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "trade", "depth", "nbEvents"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].replace(0.0, np.nan)
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        depth = data["depth"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        events = data["nbEvents"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        # Normalize each name's signed prints by its own causal activity level,
        # so the cross-sectional median is not dominated by large-cap volume.
        trade_scale = trade.abs().ewm(halflife=30.0, adjust=False).mean()
        flow = (trade / trade_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-6.0, 6.0).fillna(0.0)

        # The median suppresses idiosyncratic prints and leaves the broad shock.
        common_flow = flow.median(axis=1).fillna(0.0)
        common_impulse = common_flow.ewm(halflife=8.0, adjust=False).mean()
        common_panel = _broadcast_series(common_impulse, close.columns)

        # A name must historically participate in the broad flow shock before
        # its predicted response is used.  Negative exposures are not treated
        # as delayed transmission of the common shock.
        flow_exposure = _rolling_beta(flow, common_panel, 120).clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0)
        price_beta = _rolling_beta(ret, common_panel, 120).clip(-0.05, 0.05)

        predicted_return = price_beta * common_panel
        realized_return = ret.ewm(halflife=8.0, adjust=False).mean()
        return_scale = ret.abs().ewm(halflife=60.0, adjust=False).mean()
        response_debt = (
            (predicted_return - realized_return)
            / return_scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(-8.0, 8.0)

        # Thin depth matters only if quotes are actively changing; this avoids
        # interpreting a stale or absent book snapshot as a supply constraint.
        depth_baseline = depth.ewm(halflife=60.0, adjust=False).mean()
        sparse_queue = depth_baseline / (depth + depth_baseline).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        event_baseline = events.ewm(halflife=60.0, adjust=False).mean()
        active_book = events / (events + 0.20 * event_baseline).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        score = (
            response_debt * flow_exposure * sparse_queue * active_book
        ).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)

        return rank(score).reindex_like(close).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Common-Shock Sparse Queue Transmission
programs.trading_idea: A broad contemporaneous signed-trade shock should transmit with a delay to names whose order flow historically co-moves with that shock but whose currently sparse, active queues cannot immediately clear the implied demand or supply. The child measures the gap between each name's causally estimated return response to the common flow impulse and its realized short-run response, emphasizing active thin-book names where price formation is temporarily constrained. This is falsified if positive (negative) common-flow response debt in high-exposure sparse books does not predict positive (negative) 60-bar returns after controlling for current returns and liquidity; the edge can persist because the common shock is observable but its heterogeneous transmission through fragmented queue capacity is costly to arbitrage in real time.
programs.description: Computes a robust cross-sectional common signed-flow impulse, estimates each name's trailing flow exposure and price-response beta to that impulse, and ranks the unpriced predicted response. The signal is amplified only when current depth is low relative to its own baseline while event activity confirms that the book is actively repricing.

"""Execution-book hysteresis: delayed book adjustment reveals persistent latent execution.

Mechanism: persistent parent execution first appears in signed trades and order
flow, while effective displayed-book imbalance follows as market makers replenish
or withdraw liquidity.  A consistently positive signed-area loop in the causal
flow/book trajectory identifies this delayed relay; aligned current pressure is
then expected to continue while the execution schedule remains active.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rolling_flow_scale(frame: pd.DataFrame, window: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust magnitude scale for sparse signed event series."""
    scale = frame.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=max(12, window // 3)).median()
    return scale.replace(0.0, np.nan)


def _hysteresis_orientation(
    flow_state: pd.DataFrame,
    book_state: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bounded trailing signed area of the flow/book path.

    Positive values mean changes in flow tend to precede changes in book
    pressure under the chosen orientation.  All path increments use only t and
    t-1, and aggregation is trailing.
    """
    old_flow = flow_state.shift(1)
    old_book = book_state.shift(1)
    d_flow = flow_state - old_flow
    d_book = book_state - old_book
    increment = old_flow * d_book - old_book * d_flow
    magnitude = (old_flow * d_book).abs() + (old_book * d_flow).abs()
    signed_area = increment.rolling(window, min_periods=max(12, window // 3)).sum()
    total_area = magnitude.rolling(window, min_periods=max(12, window // 3)).sum()
    return signed_area.div(total_area.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(-1.0, 1.0)


@register_factor
class ExecutionBookHysteresisRelay(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "execution_book_hysteresis_relay"
    name = "Execution-Book Hysteresis Relay"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks directional flow/book pressure only when a trailing signed-area "
        "hysteresis loop shows that normalized signed flow has consistently led "
        "effective displayed-book imbalance."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "trade", "orderFlow", "effLobImb", "depth"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        trade = data["trade"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        order_flow = data["orderFlow"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        imbalance = data["effLobImb"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        depth = data["depth"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)

        trade_z = trade.div(_rolling_flow_scale(trade, 60)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        order_z = order_flow.div(_rolling_flow_scale(order_flow, 60)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        raw_flow = (0.65 * trade_z.fillna(0.0) + 0.35 * order_z.fillna(0.0)).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        depth_base = depth.rolling(120, min_periods=30).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        depth_ratio = depth.div(depth_base).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        depth_weight = depth_ratio.clip(lower=0.25, upper=2.0).div(2.0).fillna(0.5)

        flow_state = raw_flow.ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
        book_state = (imbalance * depth_weight).ewm(halflife=3, adjust=False, min_periods=3).mean()
        orientation = _hysteresis_orientation(flow_state, book_state, 36).fillna(0.0)

        direction = 0.70 * flow_state + 0.30 * book_state
        aligned = (np.sign(flow_state) == np.sign(book_state)).astype(float)
        active_flow = flow_state.abs().rolling(12, min_periods=4).mean().clip(0.0, 3.0).div(3.0)
        relay_strength = orientation.clip(lower=0.0) * aligned * active_flow.fillna(0.0)

        signal = (direction * relay_strength).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        return rank(signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Execution-Book Hysteresis Relay
programs.trading_idea: Persistent institutional execution creates a hysteresis loop: signed trades move first, while displayed-book imbalance adjusts with a repeatable delay as liquidity providers replenish or withdraw quotes. A positive oriented loop indicates that current book pressure is being mechanically relayed from earlier directional trading rather than being a contemporaneous noise shock; the child follows the currently aligned flow direction only in that state. The hypothesis is falsified if positive trade-to-book phase lag does not predict same-direction 60-bar returns after conditioning on current trade and book-imbalance signs. The edge should persist because latent parent-order schedules and delayed quote replenishment are costly to infer from isolated bars and cannot be instantaneously arbitraged without taking adverse-selection and inventory risk.
programs.description: Measures the causal signed area of the smoothed trade/order-flow and effective-book-imbalance trajectory, a bounded hysteresis statistic identifying whether flow systematically leads book pressure. It takes directional exposure only when the loop has the predicted orientation and current flow and book pressure agree.

"""Persistent marked cost excitation: detect unfinished adverse-selection flow.

Mechanism: execution costs that are both directionally coherent and persistent
under a slow decay kernel are more likely to represent an unfinished split
metaorder than a transient quote sweep.  Dealers observe only local fills and
replenish gradually, so this latent execution schedule can continue to move
prices over the fixed medium intraday horizon.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _robust_cost_surprise(
    effective_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    quoted_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    active: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal positive surprise in effective execution cost."""
    ratio = effective_spread / quoted_spread.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    raw = np.log(ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(active)
    center = raw.rolling(120, min_periods=30).median()
    mad = (raw - center).abs().rolling(120, min_periods=30).median()
    scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    surprise = ((raw - center) / scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)
    return surprise.fillna(0.0).where(active, 0.0)


def _persistent_marked_excitation(
    wedge: pd.DataFrame,
    signed_flow: pd.DataFrame,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Slow marked-flow kernel with a directional-coherence requirement.

    The slow kernel represents remaining metaorder pressure.  Dividing its
    signed intensity by its absolute marked intensity suppresses alternating
    flow, while comparison of short and long wedge kernels requires that the
    execution-cost state is still unusually elevated.  All kernels are causal.
    """
    marked_impulse = wedge * signed_flow
    slow_signed = marked_impulse.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    slow_abs = marked_impulse.abs().ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    coherence = (slow_signed.abs() / slow_abs.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.0, 1.0)

    short_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=18, adjust=False, min_periods=12).mean()
    long_cost = wedge.ewm(halflife=90, adjust=False, min_periods=30).mean()
    sustained_elevation = (short_cost / long_cost.replace(0.0, np.nan) - 1.0)
    sustained_elevation = sustained_elevation.clip(lower=0.0, upper=3.0).fillna(0.0)

    return (slow_signed * coherence * sustained_elevation).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class PersistentMarkedCostExcitation(BaseFactor):
    factor_id = "persistent_marked_cost_excitation"
    name = "Persistent Marked Cost Excitation"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of slow, directionally coherent signed execution-cost "
        "surprises that remain elevated relative to their long-run cost state, "
        "targeting unfinished adverse-selection flow rather than isolated sweeps."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "trade", "orderFlow", "spread", "effSpread"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        order_flow = data["orderFlow"].fillna(0.0)
        quoted_spread = data["spread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective_spread = data["effSpread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        active = (volume > 0.0) & (quoted_spread > 0.0) & (effective_spread > 0.0)
        wedge = _robust_cost_surprise(effective_spread, quoted_spread, active)

        trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        flow_scale = order_flow.abs().rolling(60, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
        trade_component = np.tanh(trade / trade_scale).fillna(0.0)
        flow_component = np.tanh(order_flow / flow_scale).fillna(0.0)
        signed_flow = (0.60 * trade_component + 0.40 * flow_component).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        excitation = _persistent_marked_excitation(wedge, signed_flow).where(active)
        signal = rank(excitation).fillna(0.5)
        return signal.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
programs.name: Persistent Marked Cost Excitation
programs.trading_idea: A single effective-versus-quoted spread wedge can reflect temporary quote noise or a completed liquidity sweep, explaining why the parent edge decays before the fixed 60-bar horizon. This child identifies wedges that remain elevated and directionally coherent under a slow exponential order-flow kernel, which is consistent with an unfinished split metaorder repeatedly consuming liquidity rather than a one-bar shock. The edge should persist because the parent order and its remaining schedule are latent to outside traders, while dealers replenish and reprice only gradually; it is falsified if persistent marked excitation has no more 60-bar continuation than an equally sized isolated cost wedge.
programs.description: Computes a robust effective-to-quoted execution-cost surprise, signs it with normalized trade and limit-order flow, and retains only directionally coherent slow-kernel excitation whose cost wedge remains elevated relative to a long baseline. The cross-sectional rank is positive for persistent buy-side adverse-selection pressure and negative for persistent sell-side pressure.

programs.code:
"""An effective spread substantially above the displayed quoted spread indicates that aggressive traders are consuming liquidity beyond what the terminal quote suggests, exposing adverse-selection pressure that passive quotes have not fully incorporated. When this execution-cost wedge is aligned with signed trades, orderFlow, and book imbalance, dealers should subsequently reprice in the aggressor's direction rather than continue supplying stale liquidity. The other side is market makers quoting from lagged or incomplete depth information; the hypothesis is rejected if high signed cost wedges are followed by symmetric reversal after controlling for spread and activity."""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _robust_positive_cost_wedge(
    effective_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    quoted_spread: pd.DataFrame,
    active: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal robust z-score of the log effective-to-quoted cost ratio."""
    ratio = effective_spread / quoted_spread.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    raw_wedge = np.log(ratio).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).where(active)

    median = raw_wedge.rolling(window, min_periods=20).median()
    deviation = (raw_wedge - median).abs()
    mad = deviation.rolling(window, min_periods=20).median()
    robust_scale = (1.4826 * mad).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    z_wedge = ((raw_wedge - median) / robust_scale).clip(lower=0.0, upper=6.0)
    return z_wedge.fillna(0.0).where(active, 0.0)


def _signed_pressure_agreement(
    trade: pd.DataFrame,
    order_flow: pd.DataFrame,
    lob_imbalance: pd.DataFrame,
    effective_lob_imbalance: pd.DataFrame,
    window: int,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Scale signed flow channels causally and form a directional consensus."""
    trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)
    flow_scale = order_flow.abs().rolling(window, min_periods=20).median().replace(0.0, np.nan)

    trade_signal = (trade / trade_scale).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
    flow_signal = (order_flow / flow_scale).clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
    lob_signal = lob_imbalance.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)
    effective_lob_signal = effective_lob_imbalance.clip(lower=-1.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

    consensus = (
        0.35 * trade_signal
        + 0.30 * flow_signal
        + 0.15 * lob_signal
        + 0.20 * effective_lob_signal
    )

    # Magnitude-squared attenuation rewards agreement and suppresses conflicted flow.
    return consensus * consensus.abs()


@register_factor
class EffectiveQuoteCostPressure(BaseFactor):
    """Signed effective-versus-quoted execution-cost pressure under fragile liquidity."""

    factor_id = "effective_quote_cost_pressure"
    name = "Effective-versus-Quoted Cost Pressure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Cross-sectional rank of a robust effective-spread-to-quoted-spread "
        "wedge signed by agreement among trades, order flow, and visible book "
        "pressure, with additional weight for declining depth and weak trade liquidity."
    )
    window_length = 60
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "volume",
        "trade",
        "orderFlow",
        "spread",
        "effSpread",
        "lobImb",
        "effLobImb",
        "trdLiq",
        "depth",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"].fillna(0.0)
        trade = data["trade"].fillna(0.0)
        order_flow = data["orderFlow"].fillna(0.0)
        quoted_spread = data["spread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        effective_spread = data["effSpread"].fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        lob_imbalance = data["lobImb"].fillna(0.0)
        effective_lob_imbalance = data["effLobImb"].fillna(0.0)
        depth = data["depth"].fillna(0.0)
        trade_liquidity = data["trdLiq"].fillna(0.0)

        active = (
            (volume > 0.0)
            & (quoted_spread > 0.0)
            & (effective_spread > 0.0)
        )

        wedge = _robust_positive_cost_wedge(
            effective_spread,
            quoted_spread,
            active,
            60,
        )
        agreement = _signed_pressure_agreement(
            trade,
            order_flow,
            lob_imbalance,
            effective_lob_imbalance,
            60,
        )

        prior_depth = depth.shift(1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        depth_change = (depth / prior_depth - 1.0).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        depth_stress = (-depth_change).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        liquidity_baseline = trade_liquidity.rolling(60, min_periods=20).median()
        liquidity_deficit = (
            (liquidity_baseline - trade_liquidity)
            / liquidity_baseline.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        ).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0).fillna(0.0)

        fragility_multiplier = 1.0 + 0.50 * depth_stress + 0.50 * liquidity_deficit
        pressure = (wedge * agreement * fragility_multiplier).where(active)

        return rank(pressure).fillna(0.5).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

programs.trading_idea: An effective spread substantially above the displayed quoted spread indicates that aggressive traders are consuming liquidity beyond what the terminal quote suggests, exposing adverse-selection pressure that passive quotes have not fully incorporated. When this execution-cost wedge is aligned with signed trades, orderFlow, and book imbalance, dealers should subsequently reprice in the aggressor's direction rather than continue supplying stale liquidity. The other side is market makers quoting from lagged or incomplete depth information; the hypothesis is rejected if high signed cost wedges are followed by symmetric reversal after controlling for spread and activity.
programs.description: Compute a robust effective-spread-to-quoted-spread wedge, suppressing zero-spread and inactive bars, then sign it by a weighted agreement of trade, orderFlow, lobImb, and effLobImb. Emphasize wedges occurring with falling depth or low trade-side liquidity and cross-sectionally rank the signed pressure score.

"""Persistent thin-side replenishment pressure under sparse liquidity.

Mechanism: persistent signed trades should have delayed price impact when the
queue on the opposite side of the book remains below its own normal capacity.
A depleted contra-side queue indicates constrained replenishment and dealer
inventory risk, distinguishing unfinished execution pressure from a transient
trade imbalance.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _safe_ratio(numerator: pd.DataFrame, denominator: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Elementwise ratio with sparse-book and divide-by-zero protection."""
    return numerator.div(denominator.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class PersistentThinsideReplenishmentPressure(BaseFactor):
    """Continuation from persistent flow facing an unreplenished contra queue."""

    factor_id = "persistent_thinside_replenishment_pressure"
    name = "Persistent Thin-Side Replenishment Pressure"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "Ranks persistent normalized signed trade multiplied by depletion of "
        "the opposite-side top queue relative to its trailing capacity, with "
        "an event-activity reliability gate."
    )
    window_length = 120
    inputs = ["close", "trade", "depth", "lobImb", "nbEvents"]
    prediction_horizon = 60
    suggested_horizons = [60]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        trade = data["trade"].astype(float).fillna(0.0)
        depth = data["depth"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)
        imbalance = data["lobImb"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)
        events = data["nbEvents"].astype(float).fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0)

        # Normalize each name's signed trades by its own typical print size.
        trade_scale = trade.abs().rolling(120, min_periods=40).median()
        normalized_trade = _safe_ratio(trade, trade_scale).fillna(0.0).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # A 12-bar decay retains execution programs while rejecting isolated prints.
        signed_pressure = normalized_trade.ewm(
            halflife=12, adjust=False, min_periods=8
        ).mean().clip(-3.0, 3.0)
        absolute_pressure = normalized_trade.abs().ewm(
            halflife=12, adjust=False, min_periods=8
        ).mean()
        coherence = _safe_ratio(signed_pressure.abs(), absolute_pressure).fillna(0.0).clip(0.0, 1.0)

        # Reconstruct best bid and ask capacities from total top depth and imbalance.
        bid_depth = (0.5 * depth * (1.0 + imbalance)).clip(lower=0.0)
        ask_depth = (0.5 * depth * (1.0 - imbalance)).clip(lower=0.0)
        bid_normal = bid_depth.rolling(120, min_periods=40).median()
        ask_normal = ask_depth.rolling(120, min_periods=40).median()

        bid_ratio = _safe_ratio(bid_depth, bid_normal)
        ask_ratio = _safe_ratio(ask_depth, ask_normal)
        contra_ratio = ask_ratio.where(signed_pressure >= 0.0, bid_ratio)
        depleted_contra = (1.0 - contra_ratio).clip(lower=0.0, upper=1.0)
        valid_queue = contra_ratio.notna() & (depth > 0.0)
        depleted_contra = depleted_contra.where(valid_queue, 0.0).fillna(0.0)

        # Require active quote formation; stale or nearly empty event bars are unreliable.
        event_normal = events.rolling(120, min_periods=40).median()
        activity_gate = _safe_ratio(events, event_normal).clip(0.0, 2.0).div(2.0).fillna(0.0)

        signal = signed_pressure * coherence * depleted_contra * activity_gate
        return rank(signal).reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.5)
programs.name: Persistent Thin-Side Replenishment Pressure
programs.trading_idea: Persistent one-sided trading is informative only when the liquidity on the opposite side of the book remains depleted relative to its own recent capacity: this identifies an unfinished metaorder interacting with constrained replenishment rather than a transient trade imbalance. Under sparse-liquidity price formation, dealers cannot immediately restore the thin queue without taking inventory risk, so the propagator from persistent signed flow should continue to move prices over the next ten minutes. This is falsifiable: conditional on equally persistent signed trade, the signal should predict same-direction returns only in names with depleted contra-side depth, and should fail or reverse when that queue has replenished.
programs.description: The signal estimates persistent normalized signed trade, measures whether the depth opposing that pressure is below its trailing median, and gates the result by contemporaneous book-update activity. It ranks names with sustained buy pressure against a thin ask queue highest and sustained sell pressure against a thin bid queue lowest.
